newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan end-February forex reserves at US$88.63 bln.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan end-February forex reserves at US$88.63 bln.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign exchange reserves rose to US$88.63 billion at the end of February compared to US$88.393 billion at the end of January, the central bank said on Tuesday.
It gave no interpretation of the relatively small rise.

Taiwan's foreign exchange reserves, the world's third largest after Japan's and China's, fell in late 1995 and early 1996 as political tensions with rival China intensified into a military crisis in march, triggering heavy capital outflows.
The trend reversed after Taiwan's March 23 presidential election and a clear easing of tensions with China, rising lowly but steadily since April.
Beijing held war games and missile tests in the Taiwan Strait in the run-up to the presidential poll, triggering waves of U.S. dollar buying and a run on gold.
The central bank intervened during the crisis to support the Taiwan dollar and the island's hypersensitive stock market.
Taiwan's foreign reserves peaked 19 months ago at $100.412 billion in June 1995, just as tensions with China erupted over President Lee Teng-hui's controversial private visit to the United States.
Note - Foreign currency reserves in billions of U.S. dollars.
